purpose: Ungraded evidence set for an independent reviewer of Korean pedestrian routing coverage. Nothing in this file is a pass or a fail.

method.engine: Pinned GraphHopper jar started on loopback through startEngine / graphhopperJavaArguments (runbook launch), on a byte-identical temporary copy of the deployed graph verified against the same manifest. The deployed graph directory was only read.
method.requestPath: Production WalkingRouteService + GraphHopperRoutingAdapter (default limits: snap 120 m, deadline 8 s, 1,000,000 visited nodes). Admission window widened to 1000/60 s so one sequential run is not refused; concurrency 1.
method.supplementaryRequest: One direct loopback /route request per pair with details road_class, road_environment, road_access, surface, used for snap distances of failed pairs and per-class metres. road_access is GraphHopper 10.0 car-oriented (motorcar, motor_vehicle, vehicle, access), not foot access.
method.tagCheck: Ways tagged foot/access (and route=ferry), foot/access/barrier nodes and military areas exported from the same extract with osmium. A route segment counts as running along a way when its midpoint is within 1.5 m of a way segment and the directions differ by at most 20 degrees. A route vertex within 1 m of a tagged node counts as passing it. A military area counts when a route segment midpoint lies inside it. These are geometric matches against OSM tags, not ground truth.
method.coordinates: Synthetic, rounded points at public landmarks chosen by hand; approximate on purpose. No personal GPS data.

deployment.note: Deployment built outside .geo-build in a persistent directory. Whether it is the one being served is stated by the node that ran this probe (the report's file name and progress record), not by this file. The default layout .geo-build/routing-graph holds c57f12f5975347e8.
